article.title: NFL EDGE Wednesday Evening Brief
article.dek: The final injury report is out — five Patriots ruled out, the Bears lose their young back but keep their right guard — and the board has refreshed to a full Week 7.

items.headline: Final injury report is out: Patriots down five, Bears down two starters
paragraphs: Thursday's game is a day away and the report is no longer a guess. New England ruled out five: starting guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown, cornerback Carlton Davis for a third straight game, and depth corners Karon Prunty and Channing Canada. Four more are questionable, including right tackle Morgan Moses and safeties Kevin Byard and Craig Woodson. Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse start at guard.

Chicago ruled out running back Kyle Monangai for a third straight game and linebacker Jack Sanborn. Linebacker T.J. Edwards is doubtful, corner Tyrique Stevenson questionable. The good news for the Bears: right guard Jonah Jackson practiced in full, got removed from the report, and will start.
Patriots (4-2) at Bears (4-2), Thursday at 8:15 p.m. ET from Soldier Field, on Prime Video.
items.takeaway: Short weeks turn every name into a maybe. The final report is in — price your bet against it, not Tuesday's guess.

items.headline: Weather: no factor Thursday night
paragraphs: Soldier Field at kickoff: about 61 degrees, wind around 5 mph, roughly a 9% chance of rain under mostly clear skies. That's as clean as October football gets in Chicago.
items.takeaway: Clean football weather. File it under not a factor and move on.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Thursday inside the app: model and market agree on Chicago
paragraphs: The board refreshed to Week 7 this evening — no more stale Week 6 screen. Both expected starters are confirmed: Drake Maye for New England, Caleb Williams for Chicago, with no injury flags on either.
The model has Chicago by about 2.3, right next to the board's -3. On the total, the model's number sits around 47.6, a few points under the board's 50.5.

DraftKings shows Bears -3 at -102 and the total at 50.5. FanDuel shows Bears -3 at -105. Your book's price may differ — that's exactly what Check is for: type in your book's line and price and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator for a bet/no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: The board is fresh, the model and market see the same game. Your price is the only one that matters — Check it.

items.headline: Sunday's headline cards: Minnesota for hit rate, Cleveland for balance
paragraphs: Hit Rate is the card's most-likely-to-win pick: Minnesota on the moneyline at -278 on DraftKings, Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET. The model gives the Vikings about a 78.6% chance to win, the app's evaluator about 75%. Hit rate is not profit rate — it trades value for win probability, on purpose.

Balanced is the middle ground: Cleveland on the moneyline at -124 on FanDuel, Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET. The model has the Browns around 71.9% while the price implies about 54%, giving it slightly positive expected value with medium reliability.
The Value lane has nothing tonight. It stays empty rather than force a play.
items.takeaway: Minnesota is the most likely winner. Cleveland is the strongest pick without paying too much. Either way, Check the price first.

items.headline: Learn the Game: handle vs. tickets
paragraphs: Two numbers describe where the betting is: ticket count is how many bets were placed, handle is how much money was wagered. They don't always agree — and the disagreement is the interesting part.

A hypothetical: imagine 100 bets on the Lions totaling $1,000, and 20 bets on the Packers totaling $9,000. The Lions win the ticket count. The Packers win the handle. That split tells you a small group of bigger bettors disagrees with the crowd.
Bigger money doesn't mean smarter money — it means fewer, larger opinions. Treat a tickets/handle split as decision context: it earns a closer look at the price, not an automatic bet.
items.takeaway: When tickets and handle point different ways, you know where the bigger money disagrees with the crowd. That's worth a look — never a pick by itself.

items.headline: Thursday: -3 holds all day through the final report
paragraphs: Bears -3 was the story this morning and it is still the story. DraftKings sat at Chicago -3 (-102) and FanDuel at Chicago -3 (-105) through Wednesday — the final injury report didn't nudge either book. The total held at 50.5 on both books too.

Earlier in the week was where the real move happened: the spread climbed from the -1.5 opener to -3, and the total rose from the mid-40s to 50.5, on the Bears' Week 6 form and the Patriots' mounting injury list.
If your book still shows something better than -3, or a total you like better than 50.5, that gap is yours to check — not the market's problem to fix.
items.takeaway: The final report is out and the market didn't flinch. There's no pending news left to wait for — if your book has a good number and Check says bet, bet it tonight.

items.headline: Thursday game? Thursday check.
paragraphs: The report is final, the weather is clean, the board is fresh. One move before kickoff: pull up the Thursday game, type your book's line and price into Check, and get the verdict on your actual number. Then log the result when it settles — winners and losers both. Settlement is manual, and the tracker only works if you're honest with yourself.
items.takeaway: Check the board, Check the price, log the result — the honest ledger is the whole game.
